# kernel-lab: standalone Q1_0 kernel verification

Extracts the Q1_0 x Q8_0 dot kernels out of ggml so one kernel can be built
and verified in isolation, without building llama.cpp.

## Files

- `q1_0.h` / `q1_0.c` - the kernels:
  - `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_generic` copied from `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/quants.c:127`
  - `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0` (+ `_vl256`, `_vl128`) copied from
    `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484` (`static` removed in the lab)
  - F4a: `repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64x1` (row-major blocks -> column-major 64-row
    bricks) + `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0_generic` scalar oracle (reference float-op
    order -> bit-exact vs per-row vec_dot on the original data)
  - F4b: `gemv_q1_0_64x1_q8_0` dispatcher + `_vl512` (i16m2/f32m4, premium)
    and `_vl1024` (i16m1/f32m2, fpga_l3) row-parallel RVV gemv - 3 vector
    ops per column, no reductions, no vector->scalar moves; per-row scales
    expanded fp16->fp32 with integer bit math (no zfh/zvfh, premium-safe)
  - fp16 conversion from `ggml/src/ggml-impl.h` (exact, table-free)
  - (the F2 defer-reduction candidates `_vl512`/`_vl512w` lived here until
    2026-07-22; removed - superseded by the F4 row-parallel repack)
- `test_q1_0.c` - correctness harness comparing every kernel vs the scalar
  reference; `test_repack_gemv` gates F4a bit-exact and F4b by the double-ref
  bound. Correctness only - cycles come from vsim (`vsim-demo/q1_0` rdcycle)

## Build and run

```
make host && ./test_q1_0_host            # x86: harness sanity (dispatcher==generic)
./test_q1_0_host --inject                # prove the harness detects a broken kernel
make rv64                                # cross build, static, RVV enabled
../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64  # QEMU, VLEN=512 (vl256 path)
QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=256,zfh=true,zvfh=true ../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64
QEMU_CPU=andes-ax45mpv,vlen=128,zfh=true,zvfh=true ../run-rv64-qemu.sh $PWD/test_q1_0_rv64  # vl128 path
make asm                                 # q1_0_rv64.s for LMUL/vl inspection
```

QEMU is for correctness only: qemu-user TCG charges a big fixed cost per
vector instruction, scalar instructions are nearly free, and pipeline stalls
do not exist - any timing it reports is misleading. Cycle decisions come from
vsim rdcycle (`/local/nick/vsim-workspace/vsim-demo/q1_0`, copies of these
kernels + mcycle A/B harness) or FPGA.

## What "verified" means

1. **Bit-exact gate**: RVV result == scalar reference result, compared as raw
   float bits, over random + edge data (all-0/all-1 sign bits, q8 saturated
   +-127, zero scales) at sizes 128..8192. The current RVV kernels do the
   same float ops in the same order as the reference, so 0 tolerance applies
   (build uses `-ffp-contract=off` to keep both sides unfused).
2. **Double-reference gate**: |result - double_ref| / sum(|terms|) < 1e-4.
   This is the gate a future optimized kernel must pass when it reorders the
   float accumulation (the F4 row-parallel repack kernels will) and
   bit-exactness vs the reference no longer applies. The per-group integer
   sums must still be exact.
3. **Harness self-test** (`--inject`): flip one weight sign bit, require the
   kernel result to change. A harness that passes a broken kernel is worse
   than no harness.
4. **Cross-platform checksum**: the PRNG is deterministic, so the final
   result checksum must be identical on x86 host and QEMU at every VLEN.

## Data domain constraints (match ggml, do not "fix")

- `n % 128 == 0` (QK1_0); the ggml dispatcher guarantees this.
- q8 quants in [-127, 127]: ggml Q8_0 quantization never emits -128.
  The RVV kernel's `vneg` on int8 -128 would wrap to -128 while the scalar
  reference negates in 32-bit; feeding -128 produces a false mismatch.
- No NaN/Inf scales: real quantization never produces them, and NaN payload
  propagation may differ between fp16 conversion implementations.

4	//   ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:484 vl256/vl128 kernels + dispatcher
5	//   ggml/src/ggml-common.h:180                block layouts
6	//   ggml/src/ggml-impl.h                      exact fp16<->fp32 (table-free)
7	#pragma once
8	
9	#include <stdint.h>
10	#include <stddef.h>
11	
12	#define GGML_RESTRICT restrict
13	
14	#define QK1_0 128
15	#define QK8_0 32
16	
17	typedef uint16_t ggml_half;
18	
19	typedef struct {
20	    ggml_half d;                // scale
21	    uint8_t   qs[QK1_0 / 8];   // sign bits: 1 -> +1, 0 -> -1
22	} block_q1_0;
23	
24	typedef struct {
25	    ggml_half d;                // scale
26	    int8_t    qs[QK8_0];        // quants, ggml quantizer emits [-127, 127]
27	} block_q8_0;
28	
29	_Static_assert(sizeof(block_q1_0) == sizeof(ggml_half) + QK1_0 / 8, "wrong q1_0 block size");
30	_Static_assert(sizeof(block_q8_0) == sizeof(ggml_half) + QK8_0,     "wrong q8_0 block size");
31	
32	// ---- F4: row-parallel Nx1 repack (see q1_0_rvv_tutorial.md section 5) ------
33	// 64 rows x 128 cols per brick, sign planes stored column-major so column c's
34	// 64 bits load as one vlm mask. Same bytes as 64 block_q1_0, transposed.
35	
36	#define Q1_NX1_N 64  // rows per brick; fp32 lanes: VLEN=512 m4 / VLEN=1024 m2
37

39	    ggml_half d[Q1_NX1_N];                 // per-row scales
40	    uint8_t   qs[QK1_0][Q1_NX1_N / 8];     // [column][row bits], 8 bytes/column
41	} block_q1_0_64x1;
42
